chunks: Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

If a man accuses his wife, then declares himself to be lying, the prescribed punishment is administered to him and she remains his wife. But if he does not declare himself to be lying, they engage in liʿān, and separation is made between them.

key_terms.أَكْذَبَ نَفْسَهُ: declared himself to be lying in his accusation
key_terms.تَلَاعَنَا: the husband and wife performed mutual imprecation (liʿān)
key_terms.جُلِدَ الْحَدَّ: the prescribed hadd punishment was carried out on him
key_terms.قَذَفَ: falsely accused of adultery or unchastity
key_terms.يُفَرَّقُ بَيْنَهُمَا: the two are separated by legal ruling

ai.seo_question: What happens in Islamic law if a husband accuses his wife and then retracts or persists in the accusation?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal ruling for a husband who accuses his wife of unchastity. If he retracts and admits his falsehood, he receives the prescribed hadd punishment and the marriage remains intact; if he does not retract, the process of liʿān takes place and the spouses are separated.
